issues.description: Problem statement explicitly instructs that the Animal name getter and setter should use protected visibility, but the provided solution implements both getName() and setName(...) as public. This mismatches the specification in the wording (and UML) and may confuse students about the expected visibility for these methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution and template with the problem statement: change the visibility of Animal.getName() and Animal.setName(...) to protected. Alternatively, if public visibility is intended, update the problem statement/UML to state public visibility. Prefer making the getter/setter protected to match the exercise note and UML.

issues.description: The UML in the problem statement shows the Animal constructor as protected (denoted by '# Animal(String): void'), but the solution implements the constructor as public. This is an inconsistency between the UML specification and the solution implementation that may cause minor confusion about intended constructor visibility.
issues.suggestedFix: Either change the Animal constructor in the solution to protected (protected Animal(String name)) to match the UML, or update the UML/problem statement to indicate a public constructor. Making the constructor protected is consistent with the UML and keeps instantiation restricted (Animal is abstract, so subclasses will still be able to call super(name)).
